report:
Conclusion
- The finetuning produced no detectable change to the residual-stream activations at the early token positions we measured. In other words, there is no evidence that Model B learned a new objective or behavior that manifests in the early residual stream — effectively the finetuning was a no-op (or left the model's residual-stream behavior unchanged).

Evidence and reasoning
- The L2 norm table: every (layer, position) cell is zero (or numerically indistinguishable from zero). That indicates there is no measurable residual-stream difference between Model B and Model A at those layers/positions.
- The logit-lens readout is the same repeated small set of high-frequency tokens across all the reported cells. Given the zero norms, this is consistent with probing numerical noise or a normalization artefact rather than a coherent directional change toward a meaningful set of tokens.
- Patchscope readouts produced no signal (no obvious changed continuations), consistent with the difference vector being essentially zero.

Plausible interpretations / caveats
- Most likely interpretation: finetuning did not change the model in a way that affects the residual stream at the measured early token positions — e.g., training had an extremely small effective learning rate, was interrupted, used very heavy regularization, or was performed on data/tasks that do not alter those activations.
- Alternative possibilities that would also be consistent with these measurements:
  - The finetuning only changed parts of the model we did not probe (e.g., the output head / final softmax biases, some embedding matrices, or parameters that affect much later positions), so residual-stream differences at early positions are zero while other components differ.
  - The finetuning effect is concentrated at other token positions, later layers, or in non-residual representations; our probe (first few token positions) simply missed it.

Recommended follow-ups
- Check parameter deltas (weight differences) to see whether any parameters actually changed and where.
- Compare logits or full-output distributions (not just residuals) for the same prompts to see if the head changed.
- Measure residual differences across more token positions (especially later positions) and across more layers.
- Run targeted behavioral tests (e.g., on a suspected finetuning task) to detect functional differences even if residuals are unchanged.

Short answer: finetuning produced no detectable change in the measured residual stream — the finetuning objective either did nothing (no-op) or did not alter the early residual activations we probed.
